# Coding Standards & Rules
- Always write clean code in logic modules, classes, and folders that are sized for human-readable maintenance. 
- Do not create or grow single large classes or source files.
- Split code into focused files, types, and modules before it becomes a catch-all implementation.
- Clean architecture means functional module/class design, not mechanical file splitting.
- don't add copyright notices
- Always write complete working code, never partial snippets.
- Preserve existing coding style where practical.
- Document the code. Explain function/modules/classes as comments.
- Keep UI design clean and clear. No redundant info or comments in the UI.
- Always create tooltips for input fields.
- Always write performant code. Do no unnecessary updates or repeated data processing. Do updates/processing on demands and bundle updates/processing.
- Write algorithms that can handle big data loads, no simple implmentations that do not perform under load.
